title: Kernel Snapshot Observability Contract and Diagnostic Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This page defines the Kernel Snapshot Observability Contract used by the serving runtime to capture lightweight, deterministic kernel-level state for fast post-hoc diagnostics, profiling correlation, and benchmark reproducibility. The contract describes snapshot contents, TTL/retention semantics, collection cadence, storage indexing, query semantics, and the recommended operational playbook for using snapshots during incidents and regressions.

Why we need a formal contract:
- Reduce triage time: snapshots provide a small, self-contained view of kernel scheduling state across shards without requiring full traces.
- Reproducible regression hunts: standardized fields make automated delta comparison (hashes/digests) possible across releases and benchmarks.
- Safe production capture: contract enforces size and cost limits to keep collection cheap and non-disruptive.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: GPU-scheduling kernels, kernel selector hints, active batch queue heads, kvcache hot entries metadata, and per-request token-progress markers. Not intended to replace full GPU traces or perf counters.
- Goals: <= 2KB compressed per snapshot per shard typical, capture latency < 5ms end-to-end, snapshot ingestion availability 99.9%.

Contract: snapshot manifest fields (string names and semantic description)
- manifest_type: "kernel-snapshot-v1" (identifies schema version).
- timestamp_utc: RFC3339 string (origin of capture).
- host_id: runtime host identifier (short hash).
- shard_id: logical shard name/id.
- kernel_hint: canonical kernel name in scheduler (e.g. "attn_sharded_kv_v2").
- active_requests: comma-separated list of up to 8 request_ids with short metadata (see Active Request Encoding below).
- batch_head_shape: concurrency/sequence-length tuple (e.g. "concurrency=12;avg_seq=128").
- kv_hot_prefix_digest: 64-bit hex digest of most-frequent KV prefixes (comma-separated up to 4).
- queue_depth: integer (number of queued kernel tasks).
- slot_usage_pct: integer 0-100 (measured GPU slot occupancy estimate).
- mem_watermark_mb: integer (resident MB attributed to shard at capture).
- fallback_flags: short tokenized list of active degradation flags (e.g. "quantized-fallback,eviction-throttle").
- capture_id: uuid string (unique id for this snapshot).
- sample_hash: sha1 hex of the canonicalized manifest (for fast equality checks).

Active Request Encoding (embedded): up to 8 items, each encoded as colon-separated tokens: request_id|model:ver|priority|est_remaining_tokens
Example: "r1234|redwood/7b:2026-03-01|p2|est32"

Size and performance constraints:
- Uncompressed manifest must be <= 8KB. Producers MUST gzip the payload before upload.
- Capture must be non-blocking for request latency: producers should sample at scheduling safe points (e.g. pre-dispatch / post-eviction) and limit synchronous work to timestamping and copying small metadata.
- Max capture cadence per shard: 1 snapshot / 5s by default; bursts up to 1/second allowed during active debugging windows.

Capture lifecycle and TTL semantics:
- Local ephemeral cache: snapshots are kept in-memory for 30s to enable immediate correlation with live traces.
- Short-term storage: snapshots forwarded to an indexed store with 7-day retention for operational triage.
- Long-term archive: on-demand (by capture_id or sample_hash) snapshots older than 7 days may be kept in cold archive for 90 days if pinned by a runbook or regression alert.
- Automatic eviction: snapshots exceeding store quotas are evicted by oldest-first per-host.

Storage & indexing conventions:
- Index keys: sample_hash, capture_id, host_id, shard_id, kernel_hint, timestamp_utc.
- Tags: release_tag (e.g. "canary-2026-03-10"), experiment_id (if collection was triggered by an experiment), incident_id (if captured during an incident).
- Searchable fields must be text-tokenized and exact-match filterable for sample_hash and kernel_hint.

Producer responsibilities and API contract:
1) Capture API (local agent): POST /v1/internal/kernel-snapshot 
   - Headers: X-Host-ID, X-Shard-ID, X-Capture-Src (auto|manual|diag).
   - Body: gzip'd manifest (UTF-8).
   - Response: 202 Accepted with JSON {"capture_id":"...","sample_hash":"...","ingest_ts":"..."}.
2) Backoff: if remote ingestion errors with 5xx more than 3 consecutive times, agent falls back to local retention only and emits metric runtime.snapshot.ingest.failures.
3) Priority: manual-triggered captures (via runbook) should include X-Capture-Priority: high and are exempt from per-shard cadence limits for a 60s window.

Query and diagnosis workflow (runbook):
1) Triage start: on a latency SLO violation or kernel regression alert, runbook owner initiates "snapshot-hunt".
2) Retrieve matching snapshots by filter: sample_hash, kernel_hint, timeframe, release_tag.
3) Run a delta comparison on sample_hash across canary vs baseline to find divergence.
4) If sample_hash matches but incident persists, escalate to full trace capture: enable continuous tracing for affected shards (see profiling-playbook integration below).

Integration with profiling playbooks and benchmarking suite:
- Profiling correlation: snapshots are lightweight keys to join streaming traces and microbenchmarks. Include capture_id in trace span attribute: runtime.kernel_snapshot.capture_id.
- Benchmark gating: nightly benchmarks must capture a deterministic snapshot for each workload and store sample_hash in benchmark results CSV. Regression rule: any benchmark run where the sample_hash distribution differs from baseline for > 20% of shards triggers a quality alert.
- Kernel scheduler experiments: when rolling out kernel changes, collect snapshot cohorts (baseline/canary) and run a pairwise hash-difference analysis as part of the release checklist.

Release gating checklist (minimum):
- Collect cohort snapshots for baseline and canary for 24 hours with at least 1000 snapshots per cohort.
- Run automated sample_hash cluster analysis and ensure no new kernel_hint set appears in >5% of canary shards unless intentionally rolled out.
- Verify average slot_usage_pct and queue_depth remain within +/- 10% of baseline.
- Sign-off required by runtime-scheduling and profiling owners.

Alerting and SLOs:
- Metric: runtime.snapshot.ingest.latency_p50 < 30ms, p95 < 100ms.
- Metric: runtime.snapshot.size_bytes_p95 < 4096 bytes compressed.
- Alert: snapshot-ingest-error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> paging to infra-oncall.
- Alert: sample_hash-drift-score > 0.2 across canary vs baseline -> notify runtime-release-team.

Known limitations and mitigations:
- Not a full trace: snapshots are intentionally small and do not include per-kernel GPU counters. Use them to triage and then escalate to detailed tracing.
- Digest collisions: sample_hash uses sha1 of a canonicalized manifest; collisions are possible but extremely unlikely. If collision suspected, attach raw manifest comparison.
- Cost: high-frequency snapshots across all shards increase storage costs; default cadence and burst limits are enforced by agents.

Operational playbook: incident example (step-by-step)
1) Pager fires for high tail latency on model X.
2) Oncall: run "snapshot-query --kernel attn_sharded_kv_v2 --since 5m --format table" across implicated shards.
3) If sample_hash variance high between recently-deployed canary and baseline: run pairwise-diff tool and note differing fields.
4) If mem_watermark_mb spike correlates with queue_depth rise -> trigger immediate spillover rollback (see runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook).
5) Capture extended traces for 10 minutes and mark capture_ids of interest.

CLI examples and snippets:
- Query tool (example):
  # list snapshots matching kernel and timeframe
  snapshot-query --kernel "attn_sharded_kv_v2" --since "2026-05-01T12:00:00Z" --limit 200 --output json

- Minimal producer example (bash curl):
  payload=$(printf '{"manifest_type":"kernel-snapshot-v1","timestamp_utc":"%s","host_id":"h-abc123","shard_id":"s1","kernel_hint":"attn_sharded_kv_v2","active_requests":"r1|m:1|p1|est24","batch_head_shape":"concurrency=8;avg_seq=64","kv_hot_prefix_digest":"%s","queue_depth":12,"slot_usage_pct":72,"mem_watermark_mb":12288,"fallback_flags":"none","capture_id":"%s"}' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "deadbeefcafebabe" "$(uuidgen)")
  echo "$payload" | gzip -c | curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" -H "X-Host-ID: h-abc123" -H "X-Shard-ID: s1" --data-binary @- https://internal-ingest.redwood/v1/internal/kernel-snapshot

Appendix A — Example canonical manifest (pretty-printed):
{
  "manifest_type": "kernel-snapshot-v1",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-05-03T14:12:02Z",
  "host_id": "h-0a1b2c",
  "shard_id": "s1",
  "kernel_hint": "attn_sharded_kv_v2",
  "active_requests": "r1234|redwood/7b:2026-03-01|p2|est32,r1240|redwood/7b:2026-03-01|p1|est8",
  "batch_head_shape": "concurrency=12;avg_seq=128",
  "kv_hot_prefix_digest": "0x9f8e7d6c",
  "queue_depth": 4,
  "slot_usage_pct": 68,
  "mem_watermark_mb": 11876,
  "fallback_flags": "quantized-fallback",
  "capture_id": "6f8d7b2a-2a5c-4b8e-9bf0-0a1c2d3e4f5a",
  "sample_hash": "a1b2c3d4e5f6..."
}

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: Runtime Observability (oncall: #infra-runtime-observability)
- Reviewers: see metadata above.
- Escalation path: runtime-scheduling -> eng-sre -> infra-ops.

Change history and notes:
- 2026-01-12: initial draft and prototype collector written (A. Patel).
- 2026-03-18: added benchmark integration rules and sample_hash gating (M. Ivanov).
- 2026-05-03: tightened ingest latency SLO and clarified retention windows (D. Kim).

If you are implementing a producer or a diagnostic tool that uses this contract, please open a lightweight RFC in the runtime team tracker and tag runtime-observability for review.
